episodes.192260: A weak mid-level trough moved across a marginally unstable airmass across northern NY during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 24th. Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and continued into the evening hours with just a few isolated pulse-type storms that produced severe, damaging winds.
episodes.192435: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a localized downburst over the Shenandoah Valley in Virginia.
episodes.192444: A few thunderstorms produced localized gale-force wind gusts over the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.192630: A warm and humid air mass across central Pennsylvania allowed for convection along a stationary boundary in the Middle Susquehanna Valley, bringing isolated instances of severe thunderstorm wind damage during the evening hours of July 24, 2024.
episodes.192696: A stalled frontal boundary helped to spark an isolated severe thunderstorm in Surry County. Winds from this thunderstorm blew down a power line just southwest of Fairview.
episodes.192762: A cluster of strong to severe thunderstorms rolled through much of southeast Arizona resulting in flash flooding including swift water rescues and damaging winds.
episodes.192802: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain and a flash flood potential along with strong outflow gusts through Wednesday. Abundant moisture and instability were present as noted by the 0.81 PWAT reading from the 23 July 1200Z KREV sounding this morning. Sufficient clearing also helped temperatures to climb well above average for late July. Short term high-resolution HREF guidance showed an uptick in PWATs Wednesday as deeper moisture expanded northward across western NV and far northeast CA |as a ridge axis slid east with upper level southerly flow increasing ahead of a trough advancing into the Pacific Northwest. A few severe storms with gusts to 60 mph and nickel sized hail were forecasted on 23 July. But flash flooding would be the bigger concern as storms moved either slower or anchored near steep terrain and burn scars. For 24 July, mid level S/SW winds increased which increased both storm motions and shear for storm organization. SPC introduced a marginal risk for severe wind gusts near the Oregon border with similar severe weather threats for stronger outflows and blowing dust reaching the Basin and Range. While storms were expected to move faster, training storm  cells would continue to bring a heightened threat for flash flooding for areas south of I-80 with focus on the eastern Sierra into southern Lyon and Mineral counties. For 25 July, drier and more stable air confined storms to the Basin and Range where activity was forecast to be isolated but still able to produce gusty outflows and areas of blowing dust.

episodes.192895: Collapsing showers and thunderstorms resulted in strong outflow gusts well away from where they decayed the night of the 24th into the 25th. Then during the afternoon of the 25th, additional showers and thunderstorms developed and resulted in strong wind gusts across the eastern plains.
episodes.192976: Minor street flooding took place in southwest Virginia on July 24th as the result of heavy downpours associated with thunderstorms. Low level moisture was bountiful on this day, allowing evolving thunderstorms to produce enough rainfall in Buchanan County for Dismal Creek to rise out of its banks. This led to a brief period of water spilling onto the adjacent road before returning to its banks later that evening once convection diminished for the day.
episodes.192990: Slow moving thunderstorms produced localized flash flooding across the area.
episodes.193131: Sufficient moisture in combination with a shortwave impulse brushing by the area resulted in numerous strong thunderstorm wind gusts in addition to isolated instances of flash flooding.
episodes.193146: An isolated thunderstorm produced a couple of severe wind gusts.
episodes.193320: A very moist airmass (precipitable water 2-2.5 inches) combined with SW steering flow focused sea breeze and boundary mergers toward the Atlantic coast where locally heavy rainfall occurred.
episodes.193406: A cold front draped from the Mid-Atlantic states into the Ohio Valley tracked southward in the evening and overnight hours, moving through northern portions of central North Carolina. Ahead of the front, storms fired along central to eastern sections of central North Carolina. Embedded stronger storms developed over the Triangle region in the afternoon hours, producing heavy rainfall and flash flooding across Wake County.
episodes.194002: Scattered showers and thunderstorms impacted eastern New York on July 24, 2024 as a result of the passing of an upper-level disturbance. A couple of thunderstorms became severe in nature, producing severe wind gusts that contributed to several reports of tree and wire damage in the Eastern Catskills and Upper-Hudson Valley. An isolated, weak EF0 tornado was also reported near Broadalbin which also resulted in tree damage on both commercial and personal property. Locally heavy downpours lead to an isolated report of minor flooding in the Lake George area.
episodes.194052: Scattered thunderstorms through the morning dissipated for a few hours around midday. By late afternoon additional thunderstorms developed along a boundary draped across Iowa from northwest to southeast. A weak upper level shortwave provided enough lift to initiate storms along this boundary. With deep layer shear of 30-35 kts, storms were able to develop and organize. Most storms remained sub-severe, however one storm just south of the Des Moines metro produced quarter sized hail.
episodes.194053: Increasing warm air advection supported scattered convection, however the lack of surface boundary and modest parameter space prevented storms from becoming organized. A few storms developed across far southern Iowa in the warm air advection wing in the early evening. While these largely remained sub-severe,  a single storm did produce a 59 mph gust at the Lamoni ASOS. Based on the radar signature, the environment with increasing dry air aloft, and isolated nature of the report, it is suspected that this was a microburst.
episodes.194291: A broad upper trough extended from the Great Lakes to northeast Texas. An upper-level disturbance moving through the Mid-South ignited convection across the Memphis metropolitan area during the late morning hours on July 25, 2024. A very moist airmass was in place across the region with anomalous precipitable water values of over 2 inches. The thunderstorms were slow moving resulting in heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.194292: A broad upper trough extended from the Great Lakes to northeast Texas. An upper-level disturbance moving through the Mid-South ignited convection across the Memphis metropolitan area during the late morning hours on July 25, 2024. A very moist airmass was in place across the region with anomalous precipitable water values of over 2 inches. The thunderstorms were slow moving resulting in heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.194488: Thunderstorms developed across the South Carolina Midlands and moved into the Lowcountry during the late evening hours. A couple of thunderstorms became strong enough to produce gusty winds, knocking down a few trees in Colleton County.
episodes.194489: Clusters of thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia in the afternoon hours within a typical summertime environment. A few storms because strong enough to produce gusty winds.
episodes.194490: In the morning, thunderstorms developed along the land breeze just off the Charleston County coast. Later that day in the evening, inland thunderstorms moved to the east across the Charleston County coast and the adjacent coastal waters. The main threat with these thunderstorms was strong wind gusts.
episodes.194512: A shortwave trough brought a cold front through southwest Idaho. This cold front brought a significant shift in the dry and hot weather with high based thunderstorms and associated winds.
episodes.194533: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed across eastern and southeastern AZ during the afternoon hours. Deep and colliding outflows sparked new development across the lower deserts of south-central AZ during the early evening hours, including several thunderstorm clusters developing over the Phoenix metro area and producing strong to severe downburst winds. The environment that these thunderstorms developed under was characterized by MLCAPE values of over 1000 J/KG with DCAPE values in excess of 1500 J/KG, which were favorable parameters for severe downburst winds.
episodes.194560: Isolated thunderstorms formed along a surface convergence zone in the afternoon of July 25th.  One of the the storms near Glenns Ferry, Idaho spun up a brief surface based circulation into a brief land spout tornado which produced damage in Glenns Ferry.
episodes.194561: A pre-frontal trough and cold front crossing western and north central New York caused a few rounds of thunderstorms through the day on July 24, 2024. The strongest storms, reaching severe criteria, occurred with the trough as it tracked east with increased instability and shear ahead of it. While most of the thunderstorms remained below severe criteria, a few damage reports were received, including a tornado.
episodes.194577: An upper-level low triggered thunderstorms across the eastern mountains of Oregon during the afternoon and evening hours of July 24. Severe hail and damaging wind gusts were reported from the public in Grant, Union, and Wallowa Counties.
episodes.194630: Strong thunderstorms stalled across downtown Mobile and caused heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.194767: Lightning from afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze causes 1 fatality and 3 injuries near St Petersburg in Pinellas County, and a structure fire near Palmetto in Manatee County.
episodes.194799: A derecho brought widespread damage to Idaho County. Around 3,000 lightning strikes occurred from Idaho to North Dakota which contributed to new wildfire starts in the region.
episodes.194825: Hurricane force winds from a rare derecho brought widespread damage to west-central Montana. The Montana governor issued an executive order declaring a disaster in both Missoula and Mineral counties due to the extent of the damage and impact.
episodes.194837: Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the morning hours on July 25th and produced heavy rainfall across Lee County, Iowa. There were reports of 3 to 4 inches of rain that led to flash flooding in Montrose.
episodes.194918: Intense showers and thunderstorms increased in coverage across parts of the Toledo Bend Country in West Central Louisiana by mid to late morning on July 25th. Rather slow cell motions and intense rainfall rates promoted areas of heavy rainfall across these areas. In addition, a weak low pressure center and related mid-level vorticity maximum were located just to the north over Southwest to South Central Arkansas. This energy focused an axis of relatively stronger moisture convergence across areas of Northeast Texas through Northwest Louisiana. Meanwhile, MLCAPE values locally across this region increased to 1000 to 1500 J/kg. Moisture was also plentiful with precipitable water values deeply tropical in nature with magnitudes of 1.75 to 2.25 inches. As a result, isolated flash flooding reports were received around Zwolle in Sabine Parish.
episodes.194939: A frontal boundary supported scattered thunderstorms across Central New York. Ahead of the front, an unstable environment triggered rounds of repeating, heavy rain producing thunderstorms that moved over the same areas. Rainfall totals of 2-3 inches fell in less than 3 hours which contributed to localized flash and urban flooding.
episodes.195154: A moist and unstable air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s on July 24, 2024. This resulted in scattered heavy rain and flooding across portions of Central and Eastern Virginia as well as isolated severe storms across south central Virginia.
episodes.195162: A deep trough stretched across South Texas into Mexico, leading to favorable conditions for efficient rainfall over the Coastal Bend. Greatest rainfall occurred on July 25th, with over 10 falling in just 6 hours over North Padre Island and rainfall rates up to 4 an hour. Several reports of streets flooded along Padre Island and in poor drainage areas of Corpus Christi.
episodes.195171: Ample monsoon moisture and slow storm motion allowed heavy rain and flash flooding over Gila County.
episodes.195189: Deep monsoon moisture over eastern Arizona triggered a thunderstorm that produced heavy rain.
episodes.195231: A thunderstorm led to 600 power outages in Kamiah.
episodes.195243: Several 50 knot plus severe thunderstorm wind gusts occurred.
episodes.195996: At the surface, a low moved northeastward from Georgian Bay to central QC during the late morning of the 24th through late morning of the 25th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front swept eastward and southeastward from far-southwestern ON, far-western Lake Erie, and northwest OH to northwestern New England, southeastern NY, northeastern and southwestern PA, and the Mid OH River Valley. Behind the cold front, a trough axis moved generally southward across Lake Erie during the morning hours of the 25th. ||Ahead of the cold front, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms generated gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the Cleveland lakeshore as the storms encountered moderate effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively, during the afternoon of the 24th. Behind the cold front, isolated multicell thunderstorms impacted western Lake Erie during the morning of the 25th as the aforementioned surface trough axis encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear. The relatively-strong updraft of one of these storms managed to spawn a non-mesocyclonic waterspout near Cedar Point.

Hurricane force winds caused hundreds of trees, of all types, and diameters up to 2 feet wide, to be either uprooted or snapped in half along the track of the derecho from between Grangeville and Pollock, east and north towards Lolo Pass. Much of the Lochsa Corridor east of Kooskia sustained massive wind damage, and blocked access to many main and side roads. Multiple people were trapped for hours until people came to cut up the trees with chainsaws. Around 58 trees had to be cut along Forest Service road 221 southeast of Grangeville. A large willow tree fell on a house in Pollock and totaled it. A woman was injured from falling trees near Moose Creek where trees snapped off 20 feet above the ground and some damaged the ranger station there. Multiple vehicles, campers and infrastructure were either damaged or totaled at the Powell, Wendover, and Whitehouse campgrounds. The forest service estimates that 1 out of every 6 leave trees were uprooted in portions of their forest. Other impacts include: widespread power outages that lasted for days, multiple power poles damaged, at least 69 lightning-caused wildfires, 911 call center was inundated with 100s of calls, a motorcyclist was run off the road on U.S. Highway 12, and rock slides between mileposts 128 and 133 on U.S. 12. One of the lightning strikes triggered the Wye fire which turned into a large, 11,000 acre Moose Creek Complex. The emergency manager of Idaho County mentioned that some areas saw some of the worst damage they had ever experienced.

A state of emergency was declared by both the Missoula County Commission Chair and Missoula Mayor because of the unprecedented wind damage that occurred. The 80 to 100 mph winds brought thousands of trees down across the county. It wasn't just a quick gust, but rather high winds that lasted for a couple of minutes. This led to power and transmission poles breaking in half and triggering power outages that lasted for up to a week after, affecting close to 40,000 customers, many of which had to toss out spoiled food. One utility reported 80 power poles were broken across their service area with 42 of those knocked down or shattered along Mullan Road, located approximately 7 miles west of US-93. Many traffic lights did not work until two days after the event. The Missoula County 911 call center received over 600 calls with many people not getting through. The main repeater on Horseback Ridge, located southwest of Missoula, went down because of the wind and firefighters could only use line-of-sight radio communication throughout the night. Natural gas meters and natural gas lines were damaged. The DNRC gave a conservative estimate that 1,000 city trees were uprooted, splintered at the truck or suffered some other total failure. Their Missoula Campus lost 52 mature ponderosa pines, and over 25 tree species. Water conservation restrictions were put up in place because the Missoula Water was running on generators. Many parts of the city were shut down including parks and mainstem rivers due to downed power lines. Live power lines trapped many people traveling through the city, including two teenagers who sat in their car for over an hour until rescue personnel could reach them in the Lower Miller Creek area. Over a hundred homes had some sort of shingle or siding damage, and many could not get roofers to fix it until 2 months later. Portions of the Blackfoot River were closed due to downed power lines and damaged power poles and lines were also reported in the Clinton, Salmon Lake, Condon and Seeley Lake areas.

County dispatch relayed report of 4 individuals that were struck by lightning and injured while standing under a tree near downtown St. Petersburg around 5:45 pm local time. Ensuing reports detailed that all 4 individuals were teenagers, 2 females and 1 male aged 16 along with a 17 year old male, and that one of the 16 year old girls had gone into cardiac arrest. Paramedics arriving on scene were able to restore the girl's pulse before taking her to Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital in St. Petersburg, along with one of the males that had received burns, and all 4 of the individuals were ultimately taken to Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital for treatment and monitoring. Unfortunately, the 16 year old girl that had to be resuscitated on scene later succumbed to her injuries on August 19.
